tagline: Down the Panhandle on the old Black Hills stage road.
intro: US 385 comes down out of South Dakota and through Chadron, a town that once moved itself to meet the railroad. Nine miles south, Chadron State Park, Nebraska's oldest, holds a piece of the Pine Ridge escarpment under ponderosa pine. From there the highway runs south to Alliance, meets the North Platte at Bridgeport and comes into Sidney, then runs east with US 30 to Chappell before turning south for Colorado.

From 1876 until a railroad reached the Black Hills in 1887, the stage road left the Union Pacific at Sidney and went north past Courthouse and Jail Rocks, crossing the river on Clarke's Bridge, to supply the gold fields.

moments.title: Chadron
moments.text: When the railroad was laid six miles from the new town in 1884, the people of Chadron packed it up, buildings and all, and moved it to the tracks.

moments.title: Carhenge
moments.text: Outside Alliance, 39 cars sprayed gray stand in the shape of Stonehenge, dedicated at the 1987 summer solstice with a 1962 Cadillac for the heelstone.

moments.title: Courthouse and Jail Rocks
moments.text: Two buttes of clay, sandstone and volcanic ash stand 240 feet above Pumpkin Creek, called castles, a church and coffins by early travelers before Courthouse and Jail stuck.

sources.label: Nebraska Department of Transportation, Scenic Byways
